mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines an empty set?

options.B: A set containing exactly one element
options.C: A set containing infinitely many elements
options.D: A set containing all natural numbers

mcqs.explanation: An empty set, denoted by {} or Ø, is a set that has no elements at all. Option A states this definition. Options B, C, and D describe other types of sets, not the empty set.

mcqs.question: A set that has a limited number of elements which can be counted is called a:
mcqs.explanation: A finite set contains a countable, limited number of elements (e.g., {1,2,3}). Option C correctly names this type. An empty set has no elements, a singleton has exactly one, and an infinite set has unbounded elements.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes an infinite set?

options.A: A set with a finite number of elements
options.C: A set that can be put into a one‑to‑one correspondence with a proper subset of itself
options.D: A set with exactly one element

mcqs.answer: A set that can be put into a one‑to‑one correspondence with a proper subset of itself
mcqs.explanation: An infinite set has unbounded size; mathematically, it can be placed in a one‑to‑one correspondence with a proper subset of itself (e.g., natural numbers and even numbers). Options A, B, and D describe finite or empty sets.

mcqs.question: If a set contains exactly one element, it is called a:
mcqs.explanation: A set with precisely one element, such as {5}, is termed a singleton set. The empty set has none, a finite set may have any limited number, and an infinite set has unlimited elements.

mcqs.question: Consider the sets A = {2, 4, 6} and B = {6, 2, 4}. Which statement is true?

options.A: A and B are not equal because the order of elements is different
options.B: A and B are equal because they contain exactly the same elements
options.C: A is a proper subset of B but not equal
options.D: B is a proper superset of A

mcqs.answer: A and B are equal because they contain exactly the same elements
mcqs.explanation: Two sets are equal if they have precisely the same elements, irrespective of order or repetition. Hence A and B are equal. Options A, C, and D misuse the concept of order and subset relations.

mcqs.question: Set P = {x, y, z} and Set Q = {1, 2, 3}. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: P and Q are equal sets
options.B: P and Q are equivalent sets because they have the same number of elements
options.C: P is a subset of Q
options.D: P and Q are disjoint sets

mcqs.answer: P and Q are equivalent sets because they have the same number of elements
mcqs.explanation: Equivalent sets have the same cardinality (number of elements). Both P and Q contain three elements, so they are equivalent. They are not equal because their elements differ, nor is one a subset of the other, and they are not disjoint because disjointness concerns common elements, which they lack, but the key concept tested is equivalence.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a common misconception about the empty set?

options.B: It is a subset of every set
options.C: It is the same as the set containing the number zero

mcqs.answer: It is the same as the set containing the number zero
mcqs.explanation: The empty set Ø has no elements, whereas the set {0} contains one element (zero). Confusing the two is a frequent mistake. Options A, B, and D correctly describe the empty set.

mcqs.question: If a set S has exactly five elements, which of the following statements must be true?
mcqs.explanation: A set with a specific, countable number of elements (here, five) is by definition finite. Therefore option C is correct. Options A and B contradict the given size, and a singleton set has only one element.
